onboarding.titles.homePlain.en: STEP 1 OF 4 · A HOME FOR THE APP

onboarding.persona.body.en: Munder Difflin turns the CLI agent you already use into a clone of you — one that runs an office of long-running agents and keeps working while you're away. It manages everything around them: context, memory, tasks, triggers, environment, files, and integrations.

onboarding.persona.ask.en: FIRST — WHO ARE YOU? (we'll tailor the setup)

onboarding.persona.technicalDesc.en: I write code or work in a terminal. Show me CLI commands, flags, and model ids.

onboarding.persona.nonTechnicalDesc.en: I'm in marketing, sales, ops, or just starting out. Explain things in plain language.

onboarding.welcome.headline.en: YOUR CLONE AND THE FLOOR IT RUNS

onboarding.welcome.descPlain.en: Your clone runs a small office of AI workers, and you watch it all from one screen. Here's what's inside:

onboarding.welcome.desc.en: Your clone coordinates a hive of AI coding agents — persistent, watchable, all local. Here's what's inside:

onboarding.welcome.features.engines.desc.en: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Kimi, Antigravity, Qwen, OpenCode, Crush, pi, Copilot & Cursor — live agents on one floor.
Eleven AI assistants — Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Grok and more — working side by side in one shared office.

onboarding.welcome.features.clone.desc.en: Your clone runs the floor — triages requests, routes tasks, and escalates only what needs you.

onboarding.welcome.features.clone.descPl.en: Your clone, {{godName}}, takes your requests, hands work to the right agent, and only interrupts you when it matters.

onboarding.welcome.features.memory.desc.en: Each agent keeps notes, mined into a shared, searchable MemPalace.

onboarding.welcome.features.memory.descP.en: Agents remember what they've done, so they don't start from scratch every time.

onboarding.welcome.features.commandCente.en: Terminal · Floor · Memory · Activity · Tasks · Triggers in one control surface.
One dashboard to watch the work, the agents' memory, tasks, and triggers.

onboarding.welcome.features.guardrails.d.en: Per-agent token budgets, a steer→constrain→stop circuit breaker, and human approvals.
Spending limits and safety stops keep agents in check — and they can ask you before big actions.

onboarding.welcome.features.hires.desc.en: Grab a pre-configured agent from the Agent Gallery and spawn it in one click.

onboarding.welcome.features.hires.descPl.en: Hire a ready-made agent from the gallery in one click — no setup needed.

onboarding.providerBlurb.qwen.en: Qwen — runs a local Qwen model on your machine

onboarding.providerBlurb.cursor.en: Cursor Agent CLI — uses your Cursor credits (Luna, Composer, …)

onboarding.home.descPlain.en: Create a new, empty folder for the app to call home. Everything the app remembers — its own settings and your agents' memory — is stored here. Something like ~/HarnessAgents works well. We'll create it for you if it doesn't exist.

onboarding.home.desc.en: Pick a folder where the harness will keep its own files — agent metadata, logs, and any new repos you create from here. Something like ~/HarnessAgents is a fine default. We'll create it if it doesn't exist.

consequences: keep its own files — agent metadata

onboarding.home.notePlain.en: You won't need to open this folder day-to-day — it's just where the app keeps its notes so nothing is lost when you restart.

onboarding.home.note.en: Think of this as the "town hall." The harness pins agent state there so sessions can be picked back up after a restart.

onboarding.orchestrator.descPlain.en: {{godName}} is your clone — he reads your requests, breaks them into tasks, and hands them to the right agent. He's the boss of the floor; you're still the boss of him. Choose which AI engine powers him.

onboarding.orchestrator.desc.en: {{godName}} is your clone — the boss of the floor you just met. He triages your requests, assigns tasks, and manages the team, while escalating anything that genuinely needs you. Pick the engine and model that power him; give him a longer-context, higher-capability model.

onboarding.orchestrator.cliAgentPlain.en: A CLI agent is an AI coding assistant that runs on your computer — popular ones are Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (OpenAI) and Antigravity (Google Gemini). Your clone is the always-on one that runs your whole office. We recommend Claude Code on Opus 4.8 (1M). You can add or switch the others later.

onboarding.orchestrator.cliAgent.en: Each option is a CLI engine (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity/Gemini, or a local proxy like Qwen). Engines marked INSTALLED are already on this machine; INSTALLS ON FIRST RUN means the app sets it up when {{godName}} first starts. Your clone ({{godName}}) is the engine that orchestrates the whole hive. Recommended: Claude Code · Opus 4.8 · 1M. Other providers can be wired per agent later.

onboarding.orchestrator.workersOnlyHint.en: Can't drain hive mail yet, so it can't run your clone — still available when hiring workers.

onboarding.orchestrator.modelNote.en: This only sets {{godName}}'s engine. You can run other providers per agent later.

onboarding.repos.descPlain.en: Add your projects. A project is simply a folder — it can hold code, documents, notes, or any files you want your agents to work with. You can create a brand-new folder or pick an existing one, and add more anytime.

onboarding.repos.desc.en: Add the repos you want your agents to work in. Each folder becomes a project (a room on the floor) — multiple agents can share one. You can add more later.

onboarding.repos.emptyPlain.en: No projects added yet. Optional — you can add one later.

onboarding.repos.empty.en: No repos added yet. Optional, but recommended.

onboarding.permissions.autonomyHead.en: HOW MUCH CAN AGENTS DO ON THEIR OWN?

onboarding.permissions.autoLabelPlain.en: LET AGENTS WORK ON THEIR OWN

onboarding.permissions.autoOnPlain.en: On. Agents carry out tasks without stopping to ask — the smoothest experience.

onboarding.permissions.autoOffPlain.en: Off. Agents pause and ask you before changing files or running commands.

onboarding.permissions.autoOn.en: On. Agents never pause — Claude runs bypassPermissions, Codex bypasses approvals + sandbox, etc.

onboarding.permissions.autoOff.en: Off. Each agent asks before edits / shell commands (Claude default, codex -a untrusted, …).

onboarding.permissions.autoNotePlain.en: Best when agents work in their own projects. You can change this later, including for individual agents.

conditions: agents work in their own projects

onboarding.permissions.autoNote.en: The right default for the "control room" experience; a foot-gun on production repos. Override per agent in the Add Agent dialog.

onboarding.permissions.reliabilityHead.en: KEEP THINGS RUNNING WHILE YOU'RE AWAY

onboarding.permissions.reliabilityDescPl.en: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals, even when you step away. These settings keep you in the loop and keep things running.

onboarding.permissions.reliabilityDesc.en: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals. If your computer fully sleeps those timers pause and catch up the moment you're back — nothing is lost, it may just run late.

conditions: your computer fully sleeps those timers pause and catch up the moment you're back — nothing is lost

onboarding.permissions.keepAwakeDesc.en: Strong keep-alive: stops your computer from sleeping while an agent is live, so schedules and terminals fire on time even when you step away. Uses more battery — best on power. Off by default.

onboarding.permissions.notificationsDesc.en: Get pinged when an agent needs you or a terminal needs reviving — even while you're away. Your system may ask permission the first time one fires.

conditions: an agent needs you or a terminal needs reviving — even while you're away

onboarding.permissions.openAtLoginDesc.en: Relaunch the harness after a reboot so scheduled missions resume on their own. No prompt — applies immediately.

onboarding.permissions.shareStatsDesc.en: A handful of anonymous events (app opened, agent spawned, feature used) that help improve Munder Difflin — never prompts, code, file paths, or agent output. Full list in TELEMETRY.md; change anytime in Settings.

onboarding.permissions.stayAwakeDescMac.en: macOS only lets you set this one yourself. In Battery → Options, turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off" (on power adapter) so timers keep firing with the display asleep. Without a sleep-preventing setting the Mac still truly sleeps — work survives and catches up on wake.

conditions: the display is off" (on power adapter) so timers keep firing with the display asleep

onboarding.permissions.stayAwakeDescWind.en: Windows only lets you set this one yourself. In Settings → System → Power & battery → Screen, blank & sleep, set "On battery power, put my device to sleep" and "When plugged in" to Never (or increase them) so timers keep firing. Without a sleep-preventing setting Windows still truly sleeps — work survives and catches up on wake.

conditions: plugged in" to Never (or increase them) so timers keep firing

onboarding.permissions.stayAwakeDescLinu.en: Your desktop environment only lets you set this one yourself. Look for a Power Settings panel (e.g. GNOME Settings → Power, or KDE System Settings → Power Management) and disable automatic sleep/suspend while on power. Without a sleep-preventing setting your machine still truly sleeps — work survives and catches up on wake.

aiEngines.providersDesc.en: API keys + local endpoints for the OpenCode, Crush, pi.dev and Qwen engines. Keys are stored write-only (encrypted at rest; never shown again) and used only when those engines spawn. Claude Code and Codex use their own login.

mcpDefaults.desc.en: These servers are merged into each new agent's session settings. Safe servers are on by default; write/secret servers are off until you consent. Changes take effect on the next agent spawn — running agents are not affected.

mcpDefaults.tiers.safeReadonlyNote.en: These servers read data only, need no secrets, and are scoped to the agent workspace. They are enabled for every new agent.

mcpDefaults.tiers.writeNote.en: These servers can mutate state beyond the workspace. Off by default — enable only after reviewing.

mcpDefaults.tiers.secretNote.en: These servers require an API key or credentials. Off by default — add your credentials and enable after consent.

orgSection.settingsOnly.en: Settings only, for now. The org messaging service does not exist yet, so a key here starts no connection and nothing is sent or received. It is stored ready for when it does.

orgSection.noKeyWarning.en: This is switched on with no key set, so no teammate can reach you yet.

contextSection.intro.en: A rule fires only when both halves agree: the gap since its last run has passed, AND that agent's context is at least as full as the bar. A bar of 0% means the clock alone.

conditions: both halves agree: the gap since its last run has passed

contextSection.compactBlurb.en: Summarises the context so the thread keeps going.

contextSection.clearBlurb.en: Discards the context. Nothing is summarised.

contextSection.clearCaution.en: Clearing throws context away — it is not a smaller version of compaction. An agent mid-task forgets what it was doing. Leave this off unless you keep context another way.

conditions: NOT: you keep context another way

contextSection.extraFocusHint.en: Appended to the provider's compaction command. Empty sends the bare command.

contextSection.commandHint.en: Sent literally. Empty sends the bare clear command.

contextSection.contextBarHint.en: How full the window must be before this may run. 0% = time alone.

contextSection.bigWindowsHint.en: Used on ~1M-token windows, where a smaller slice is still an enormous amount of text.

schedulesSection.promptPlaceholder.en: Sent word for word on every run.

schedulesSection.beatCeiling.en: The beat adapts to how quiet the floor is, so this is the ceiling, not the exact gap.

webhooksSection.intro.en: Anyone holding a URL and its secret can post work in. Each endpoint carries its own secret, so revoking one caller leaves the others alone.

webhooksSection.newEndpointHint.en: A new endpoint starts switched off. Copy its URL and secret, then turn it on.

webhooksSection.noAddressYet.en: This endpoint has no public address yet. It appears once the tunnel picks it up.

webhooksSection.serverNotListening.en: The webhook server is not listening, so there is no address to hand out yet.

webhooksSection.secretHint.en: Callers echo this in the x-md-webhook-secret header.

webhooksSection.schemaDesc.en: what an inbound body must look like

webhooksSection.notValidJson.en: Not valid JSON — {{error}}. Nothing was saved.

triggersUi.pickDayHint.en: Pick at least one day, or this will never run.

triggerHistory.tailRejected.en: You turned this down. Nothing was sent to the hive.

triggerHistory.tailNoReply.en: No reply yet. {{godName}} has this one.

triggerHistory.pendingDirectiveDesc.en: Approve and this goes to {{godName}}, who will put the hive to work on it. Reject and it is dropped — nothing runs.

consequences: put the hive to work on it

triggerHistory.pendingDesc.en: Approve and {{godName}} reads this. Reject and it is dropped — nothing runs.

triggerHistory.rejectTitle.en: Drop this message. Nothing is sent

triggerHistory.sectionWebhooksBlurb.en: Everything posted to your webhook endpoints, next to what {{godName}} sent back.

triggerHistory.sectionOrgBlurb.en: Messages from your teammates' clone nodes, next to what {{godName}} sent back.

triggerHistory.heldOne.en: One message is held, waiting on your yes or no.

triggerHistory.heldMany.en: {{count}} messages are held, waiting on your yes or no.

triggerHistory.decideFailed.en: That did not go through. Try again.

triggerHistory.clearFailed.en: Could not clear it. Try again.

triggerHistory.emptyOrgTitle.en: Nothing here yet, and nothing is broken.

triggerHistory.emptyOrgBody.en: Teammate messaging is not built yet. You can set an org key and pick a mode today, but no one's clone node can reach yours until the transport ships. When it does, their messages and our replies land here.

triggerHistory.emptyWebhookBody.en: When something posts to one of your endpoints, it lands here with {{godName}}'s reply underneath. Nothing has called in so far. Add an endpoint under Webhooks to get a URL you can hand out.

conditions: something posts to one of your endpoints

triggerHistory.clearConfirm.en: Delete all {{count}} messages? The record is gone for good.

fileEditor.openInIdeTitle.en: Open this file in the full IDE

gitTab.notARepoHint.en: Run git init in the agent's terminal.

fullscreenTerminal.hideAgentList.en: Hide the agent list — full-width terminal

fullscreenTerminal.respawnTitle.en: Respawn from last session: {{names}} — same ids, memory and inboxes reattach automatically

fullscreenTerminal.closeAgent.en: Close {{name}} — ends the process and archives the agent

fullscreenTerminal.ideTip.en: Open the IDE: browse and edit files in {{name}}'s workspace, and see their uncommitted changes as a diff.

fullscreenTerminal.openTerminalTip.en: Open your system terminal app in {{cwd}} — a normal shell in this agent's folder, separate from the agent's own terminal.

fullscreenTerminal.openTerminalAria.en: Open a system terminal in this agent's folder

memoryPanel.openTitle.en: Search the shared memory your agents build up

memoryPanel.intro.en: What your agents remember across sessions, shared between them. Search it by meaning, not just exact words.

memoryPanel.plainNotesStill.en: Agents still keep plain notes without it.

threads.empty.en: No conversations yet. Messages this agent receives will appear here as threads.

skillsTab.categoryTitle.en: Categories as published by the catalog

skillsTab.noSkillsInstalled.en: No skills installed yet. Open Browse to see what is available.

workersTab.liveIntro.en: Isolated workers {{godName}} spins up to handle Slack messages — they run to completion, reply in-thread, then tear down.

workersTab.baseBranchTitle.en: base branch the worktree was cut from

workersTab.preservedIntro.en: Finished workers whose worktree held un-integrated work — kept (never auto-discarded) and auto-reclaimed once the work lands in its base branch.

integrations.errId.en: Could not derive a valid id from the label.

integrations.errBaseUrlFormat.en: Base URL must be https:// (or http://127.0.0.1 / localhost for a local target).

integrations.errHeader.en: Header name must be 1–64 chars of A–Z, 0–9, or "-".

integrations.galleryDesc.en: Choose what you're connecting. The template sets the defaults. Pick Custom REST for anything not listed.

integrations.secretDesc.en: Encrypted in the main process and never shown again. To change it, paste a new key — the old one can't be read back.

integrations.blankKeepsKey.en: Leave blank to keep the saved key.

integrations.addSecretToEnable.en: Add a secret and enable to make it available.

integrations.disabledNoUse.en: Disabled — no worker can use it.

integrations.v1Note.en: v1 grants every enabled integration to all workers. Per-worker scoping is coming.

integrations.testAfterSave.en: Save the integration first, then test the live connection.

integrations.testLiveDesc.en: Runs a live read-only probe against the base URL with the stored secret.

integrations.titleDesc.en: Connect outside tools so your agents can read and act on them. Secrets are stored encrypted in the main process and never shown again.

integrations.empty.en: No integrations yet. Connect GitHub or a custom REST API so your agents can use it.

kanban.newWorkHint.en: new work? dispatch it to {{godName}} (monitor tab)

kanban.needsYouTitle.en: waiting on YOUR answer — see the ASK ME tab

kanban.dismissTitle.en: dismiss this task (removes it from the board)

kanban.awaitingAnswer.en: AWAITING YOUR ANSWER — ASK ME TAB

queueComposer.heldDraft.en: held — {{name}}'s terminal has unsent text on its prompt

queueComposer.heldPicker.en: held — a slash-command picker is open in {{name}}'s terminal

queueComposer.pausedTitle.en: Auto-delivery is paused for the whole floor. Resume it in the Command Center, or use "send now" on a message below.

queueComposer.sendNowTitle.en: Deliver this message even though auto-delivery is paused. It moves to the front of the queue and types in as soon as the terminal is free.

queueComposer.ffNoKeyTitle.en: Dictation needs a free Groq API key. Click the info mark for the steps.

queueComposer.ffTitle.en: Free Flow — dictate into the queue. Click, or hold Option (⌥).

queueComposer.ffSetupIntro.en: Speak instead of typing. Groq transcribes it, and their free tier covers this — no card, no cost.

queueComposer.ffPasteKey.en: Paste it into Settings → Voice → Groq API key

queueComposer.ffClickOrHold.en: Click voice, or hold the right Option key to talk

queueComposer.ffHoldHint.en: Hold it ALONE for a moment to start; release to transcribe into the composer, where you can edit before sending. Either Option key works, and Option+key combos still reach the terminal untouched.

idePanel.workspaceInferred.en: No agent was named when the IDE opened — showing {{name}}'s workspace (the current selection)

conditions: the IDE opened — showing {{name}}'s workspace (the current selection)

idePanel.collapseGit.en: Collapse the git panel — more room for the file tree

gitPanes.jumpConfirm.en:
Jump the repo to {{sha}} ("{{subject}}")?

This detaches HEAD. Blocked automatically if the tree is dirty or an agent is mid-run.

gitPanes.switchConfirm.en:
Switch this repo to '{{head}}'?

Blocked automatically if the tree is dirty or an agent is mid-run.

gitPanes.baseTitle.en: Base — the branch you're comparing against

gitPanes.compareTitle.en: Compare — the branch whose changes you're viewing

gitPanes.modeThreeTitle.en: Showing what the compare branch ADDS since the common ancestor (PR-style). Click for the literal two-dot difference.

gitPanes.modeTwoTitle.en: Showing the literal difference between the two branch states. Click for PR-style (what compare adds).

imagePreview.fitTitle.en: Scale the image down to fit the pane

imagePreview.oneToOneTitle.en: Show every pixel at 1:1 (scroll to pan)

imagePreview.viewSourceTitle.en: Open the SVG markup in the editor

imagePreview.decodeFailed.en: could not decode this image — the file may be corrupt or misnamed
